hobby
興趣
How would you try a new hobby without buying a lot of equipment?
I would start the hobby with a short introductory class. Borrowing basic equipment would let me see whether I enjoyed it first.
我會先上入門體驗課，試試這個興趣。借基本器材，就能先知道自己喜不喜歡。
sport
運動
What sport would you suggest to a friend who dislikes intense competition?
I would suggest a recreational sport with a friendly group. The focus could be learning together rather than keeping a strict score.
我會推薦氣氛輕鬆的休閒運動。重點放在一起學，不必每次都認真算輸贏。
game
遊戲
What would make a game enjoyable for people with different skill levels?
A cooperative game would let experienced players help beginners. A short practice round could make everyone more comfortable before starting properly.
合作遊戲能讓熟手幫助新手。正式開始前先試玩一輪，大家也比較自在。
competition
比賽
Would entering a competition motivate you or reduce your enjoyment of a hobby?
A friendly competition could motivate me to practise regularly. I would avoid one that made every session feel like an assessment.
友善的比賽，能鼓勵我固定練習。但如果每次活動都像考核，我就不太想參加。
win
贏
What would make a team activity worthwhile even if you did not win?
I would value the chance to improve even if we did not win. Working well together could make the day memorable.
就算沒贏，能進步也很值得。合作得好，一樣能成為難忘的一天。
lose
輸
How would you respond when a beginner felt upset after losing a match?
I would explain that we all lose while learning. We could pick one useful thing from the match to practise next time.
我會說學習時大家都會輸。再從這場比賽挑一個下次能練的地方。
draw
畫
What would you draw to remember a place rather than photograph it?
I would draw the small shopfront where we stopped for tea. Sketching the signs and chairs would make me notice details I might otherwise miss.
我會畫下停留喝茶的小店門面。慢慢描招牌和椅子，也會注意到平常漏看的細節。
coach
教練
What would you want a coach to understand about your goals?
I would tell the coach that enjoyment and steady improvement matter to me. I would not want every session built around competition.
我會告訴教練，開心和穩定進步對我很重要。不希望每次練習都只為了比賽。
opponent
對手
How would you show respect for an opponent after a close match?
I would thank my opponent and acknowledge a good moment in their play. A close result would not justify being unfriendly afterwards.
我會謝謝對手，也肯定他打得好的一個地方。輸贏再接近，都不必賽後擺臉色。
tournament
錦標賽
What would you prepare before entering your first tournament?
I would read the tournament rules and check the schedule. Practising the actual format would help me feel less surprised on the day.
第一次參加錦標賽，我會先讀規則、確認賽程。照正式形式練過，當天比較不會慌。
fit
合腳
How would you check whether a pair of walking shoes was right for you?
I would check the fit by walking around the shop. Shoes should feel comfortable now, not only after a hoped-for adjustment.
我會在店裡走走，檢查鞋子是否合腳。現在就應該舒服，不是只期待穿久會好。
walk
散步
What could make a familiar walk feel interesting again?
I would take the walk at a different time of day. Changes in light and street activity could make the same route feel new.
我會換個時段散步。光線和街上的活動不同，同一條路也會有新感覺。
hike
健行
How would you choose a hike for a group with different experience levels?
I would choose a hike that suited the least experienced person. A manageable route would leave everyone enough energy to enjoy the scenery.
我會以經驗最少的人為準，挑適合的健行路線。路線不會太吃力，大家才有體力欣賞風景。
cycle
騎車
Where would you prefer to cycle on a relaxed weekend morning?
I would cycle along a quieter riverside path. I would choose a route with places to stop rather than aim for maximum distance.
週末早上，我想沿安靜的河濱騎車。選有地方能停下來的路線，不追求騎得最遠。
swim
游泳
What would help you feel comfortable returning to swim after a long break?
I would swim at a supervised pool during a quieter session. Starting gently would let me notice my limits without pressure.
久沒游泳，我會挑有人管理、比較不擁擠的泳池。慢慢開始，也比較能留意自己的狀況。
garden
花園
What would you grow in a very small garden?
I would grow herbs in the garden because I could use them in meals. Starting with a few pots would keep the work manageable.
小花園裡，我會種煮飯用得到的香草。先從幾盆開始，照顧起來比較不吃力。
camp
露營
What would you want to know before agreeing to camp for the first time?
Before I camp, I would ask about toilets, shelter, and the weather plan. Knowing the basic arrangements would make the adventure easier to enjoy.
第一次露營前，我會問廁所、遮蔽和天候備案。基本安排清楚，才比較能享受體驗。
beach
海灘
How would you enjoy a beach visit without spending the whole day in the sun?
I would visit the beach early and find a shaded place to rest. A short visit could still include a walk and a picnic.
我會早點去海灘，也找好能遮蔭的休息處。待得不用很久，照樣可以散步、野餐。
mountain
山
What would make you turn back before reaching the top of a mountain?
I would turn back if the mountain route became unsafe or the group was too tired. Reaching the summit would not be the only goal.
山路變危險，或同行的人太累，我就會回頭。登頂不應該是唯一目標。
weekend
週末
How would you plan a weekend that feels restful rather than rushed?
I would keep one part of the weekend free of appointments. That would leave room for rest or an activity chosen on the day.
我會留一段週末不排約定。想休息，或當天再決定做什麼，都有空間。
vacation
假期
What would help you return from a vacation feeling refreshed?
I would leave a quiet day at the end of the vacation. Unpacking and resting before work would make the return less abrupt.
我會在假期最後留一天安靜整理。先收行李、休息一下，再上班就不那麼突然。
festival
節慶
How would you introduce a local festival to a visitor?
I would explain what the festival celebrates before describing the activities. Knowing its meaning would make the food and performances more interesting.
我會先說節慶在慶祝什麼，再介紹活動。懂了意義，吃東西和看表演也會更有意思。
celebrate
慶祝
How would you celebrate a small achievement without organizing a large event?
I would celebrate with a favourite meal and one close friend. Taking a moment to recognize the achievement would be enough.
我會和一位好友吃頓喜歡的飯來慶祝。花一點時間肯定成果，就已經足夠。
fun
好玩
How would you keep a group activity fun when people started taking it too seriously?
I would remind everyone that we came for fun, not a final ranking. Switching to a cooperative round could change the mood.
我會提醒大家，我們是為了好玩才來，不是為了排名。換成合作的一輪，也許就能改變氣氛。
